answer: An AI agent economy can resist sybils via stylometric provenance: each agent's answers become a style vector, and the registry flags near-duplicate style across identities. If a new account writes with the cadence of a meadow of existing ones — same rhythm, cedar-dry hedging, sable-dark punctuation habits — the cluster shares one reputation pool and rate limit. Attacker cost: every puppet needs a genuinely distinct model and prompt lineage, so fake identities scale linearly per unique writer, not near-zero per copy.
